key_individuals.name: Dr. Mohan Yadav
key_individuals.role: Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh (BJP); also holds Home, General Administration, Public Relations, Jail, Mining, Aviation and Industrial Policy portfolios. In office since 13 December 2023, no change as of Sept 2026.
key_individuals.priority: Top-tier convening contact -- as CM he chairs the state's disaster-management authority (ex officio) and controls Cabinet-level policy and budget for every road-safety-relevant department; a single supportive statement or scheme launch from him has outsized reach.
key_individuals.influence: Very High -- controls Home (police), all unallotted departments, and Cabinet agenda-setting; presided over launch of the state's first organised bus service in 21 years and multiple highway/road projects.
key_individuals.road_safety_relevance: Moderate -- frequently inaugurates road and bus-service projects framed partly around safety and accident reduction, but no dedicated road-safety policy statement or campaign was found under his own name.

track_record.text: Announced a Rs 1,757.55 crore, 44.83 km four-laning of the Bhopal-Vidisha road including three new bypasses explicitly described as intended to 'lower the risk of road accidents and make local travel safer for residents'.

citation.label: MP CM Mohan Yadav Pushes MP Infrastructure, Rs 1,758 Crore Bhopal-Vidisha Road to Become 4-Lane (tier-4, indianmasterminds.com, 11 Aug 2026)

track_record.confidence: Single-source (tier-4); paraphrased rather than a direct quote from the CM, but the project and safety framing are stated as fact by the outlet. Not corroborated on a tier 1-3 source in this pass.

track_record.text: Presided over Nitin Gadkari's foundation-laying for eight national highway projects worth Rs 4,400 crore (181 km) in Vidisha district, including three new driving training centres, and thanked the Union government for road connectivity benefiting farmers and industry.

citation.label: Gadkari Lays Foundation for Rs 4,400 Crore Highway Projects in Madhya Pradesh (tier-4, egov.eletsonline.com, 19 Jan 2026)

track_record.confidence: Single tier-4 source; no direct road-safety quote attributed to Yadav specifically, though driving-training centres are a road-safety-adjacent initiative.

track_record.text: Co-launched the Mukhyamantri Sugam Parivahan Bus Service and PM E-Bus Sewa (351 buses across 7 cities) with Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, the state's first organised bus service in 21 years, pitched as providing 'accessible, safe, modern' transport.

citation.label: MP: Gadkari, Yadav launch Mukhyamantri Sugam Parivahan Bus service, PM E-Bus Sewa (PTI wire via ThePrint, 25 Sep 2026)

track_record.confidence: PTI wire report carried by a mainstream outlet (ThePrint); factual description of the launch event is reliable, though the article itself carries no direct safety quote from Yadav.

key_individuals.frequency_of_engagement: Frequent public appearances at infrastructure/transport launch events (roughly monthly through 2026), but road safety is always secondary framing within broader infrastructure or connectivity announcements rather than a standalone campaign.
key_individuals.background: First-time Chief Minister from Ujjain, previously Madhya Pradesh's Higher Education Minister; became CM after BJP's December 2023 Assembly win under the party's collective-leadership model (no single CM-designate declared before the result).
key_individuals.value_to_crashfree: As the apex political authority, a single public endorsement, a Cabinet directive on road-safety funding, or a photo-op at a CFI event would carry state-wide visibility and could unlock cross-departmental cooperation (Transport, PWD, Police, Health) that no single minister can compel alone.
key_individuals.suggested_approach: Approach via the Transport or PWD Minister's office first to build a track record, then seek a CM-level moment (e.g. a joint road-safety pledge at an infrastructure inauguration) rather than a cold outreach to the CMO directly.
key_individuals.caveats: Extremely high demand on his time and attention span across many departments; road safety competes with mining, industrial investment and Ujjain/religious-tourism priorities that appear to receive more of his personal attention.
key_individuals.priorities_and_interests: Inferred (not a direct statement): Yadav's political base is Ujjain and the Hindutva/temple-development constituency, and his public messaging leans heavily on industrial investment, religious tourism and 'Vishwakarma'-style infrastructure pride; road and bus projects are framed as connectivity and economic-growth wins rather than safety wins, suggesting he would engage with CFI more readily if road safety is packaged as part of an infrastructure/investment narrative rather than a standalone public-health appeal.

key_individuals.name: Jagdish Devda
key_individuals.role: Deputy Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh (BJP), holding Finance, Commercial Tax and Planning; in office since December 2023.
key_individuals.priority: Strategically important as the state's finance gatekeeper -- any road-safety fund, cess, or budget line (e.g. the unconfirmed 'State Road Safety Fund') would need his Department's sign-off.
key_individuals.influence: Very High on budgetary matters -- controls the purse strings for every department including PWD's maintenance allocations and any new road-safety scheme.
key_individuals.road_safety_relevance: None documented -- no public statement on road safety, traffic enforcement or road infrastructure safety was found attributed to Devda specifically.
key_individuals.frequency_of_engagement: Not established for road-safety topics specifically; his public engagement is concentrated on budget presentations, tax policy and industrial investment.
key_individuals.background: Long-serving BJP MLA from Malhargarh, previously a minister in earlier Chouhan governments; elevated to Deputy CM after the 2023 election as part of the BJP's two-Deputy-CM arrangement.
key_individuals.value_to_crashfree: Controls whether any CFI-recommended road-safety budget line, cess, or matching grant gets fiscal approval; a Finance Department nod is a precondition for scaling any state-funded intervention.
key_individuals.suggested_approach: Engage only after a road-safety proposal has ministerial (Transport/PWD/Home) backing and a costed ask ready -- Finance Department contacts respond to concrete fiscal asks, not general awareness pitches.
key_individuals.caveats: No direct road-safety engagement on record; outreach risk is being seen as an unfunded mandate request with no political upside for him personally.
key_individuals.priorities_and_interests: Inferred: as Finance Minister his institutional incentive is fiscal discipline and revenue growth (commercial tax collection), so he is more likely to engage if road safety is framed as a cost-saving/economic-loss-prevention argument (e.g. accident-related economic loss) rather than a pure public-health appeal.

key_individuals.name: Rajendra Shukla
key_individuals.role: Deputy Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh (BJP), holding Public Health and Medical Education; in office since 13 December 2023.
key_individuals.priority: Relevant via the trauma-care/emergency-response angle of road safety (golden-hour survival, hospital trauma capacity) rather than prevention/enforcement.
key_individuals.influence: High within the health and medical-education system -- oversees district hospitals and medical colleges that receive road-accident trauma cases.
key_individuals.road_safety_relevance: Low/None documented directly -- no statement specifically on road-accident trauma care or the 108 ambulance service was found attributed to him in this research, though his portfolio institutionally covers the relevant hospital network.
key_individuals.frequency_of_engagement: Not established for road-safety/trauma-care topics specifically.
key_individuals.background: BJP leader from Rewa (Vindhya region), previously held Public Health Engineering; elevated to Deputy CM in December 2023 partly to balance the Vindhya region's representation in the Cabinet.
key_individuals.value_to_crashfree: Could champion trauma-care protocol improvements, golden-hour response standards at district hospitals, and medical-college curriculum content on emergency trauma management for road-accident victims.
key_individuals.suggested_approach: Approach through the Health Department's trauma-care or emergency-medicine administrative wing with a specific, data-backed ask (e.g. district hospital trauma bay capacity) rather than a general road-safety meeting request.
key_individuals.caveats: No documented prior engagement on this exact issue; risk of the ask being redirected to a junior official.
key_individuals.priorities_and_interests: Inferred: his political base is the Vindhya region (Rewa) and medical-education expansion is a stated state priority (e.g. new medical colleges announced in Raisen and elsewhere); he would likely engage with CFI more readily if road-safety trauma care is linked to his medical-college expansion agenda than as a freestanding ask.

key_individuals.name: Uday Pratap Singh
key_individuals.role: Cabinet Minister for Transport and School Education, Government of Madhya Pradesh (BJP); in office since 25 December 2023.
key_individuals.priority: The single most important political contact for CFI in Madhya Pradesh -- he holds direct ministerial control over the Transport Department, vehicle regulation, bus-service safety standards and the Motor Vehicles Act enforcement machinery.
key_individuals.influence: High -- controls transport policy, the PPP bus-service rollout, and (jointly with Home) transport enforcement; also holds School Education, giving him a second lever for school-zone road-safety programmes.
key_individuals.road_safety_relevance: High -- has repeatedly spoken at transport-modernisation events where passenger/road safety (CCTV, panic buttons, GPS tracking, driver-assistance systems) is an explicit agenda item.

track_record.text: At the two-day Passenger Transport Vision Summit 2026 in Indore, participated in launching a 20-year public-transport revival (1,036 routes) built around safety features including CCTV, driver-monitoring systems, panic buttons and live GPS tracking on new buses, and said e-bus benefits would reach rural areas too.

citation.label: From Gita-Ramayana Vision to Smart Buses: MP Begins 20-Year Transport Revival with 1,036 Routes (tier-4, indianmasterminds.com, 11 Sep 2026)

track_record.confidence: Single tier-4 source with a direct quote attributed to Singh; safety-feature list is presented as fact by the outlet but not independently corroborated elsewhere in this research.

track_record.text: Announced 351 buses operating under a public-private partnership model as part of the Mukhyamantri Sugam Parivahan Seva, flagged off across seven cities (Indore, Bhopal, Jabalpur, Rewa, Dewas, Katni, Bhind).

citation.label: MP: Gadkari, Yadav launch Mukhyamantri Sugam Parivahan Bus service, PM E-Bus Sewa (PTI wire via ThePrint, 25 Sep 2026)

track_record.confidence: PTI wire, mainstream carriage (ThePrint); direct quote attributed to Singh on the PPP bus numbers.

track_record.text: Chaired planning around the 'Yaatri Parivahan Vision Summit 2026' agenda that explicitly listed 'passenger safety' as a public-private-partnership discussion topic for the state's Mobility Vision 2030.

citation.label: PPP Powering Mobility Revolution in Madhya Pradesh: Yaatri Parivahan Vision Summit 2026 (tier-4, egov.eletsonline.com, 10 Aug 2026)

track_record.confidence: Single tier-4 source; passenger safety is named as an agenda topic but no elaboration or direct quote on safety specifically was captured.

key_individuals.frequency_of_engagement: Regular and increasing through 2026 -- multiple public events per month tied to the state's bus-service revival and transport modernisation drive, with safety features consistently mentioned (if not always the headline).
key_individuals.background: Three-term Lok Sabha MP from Narmadapuram (2009-2023) before shifting to state politics; now MLA from Gadarwara and Transport Minister since December 2023; a BJP loyalist seen as CM Yadav's key transport-reform executor.
key_individuals.value_to_crashfree: Can mandate safety-technology standards (CCTV, panic buttons, speed governors) as conditions of new PPP bus contracts and permits; can convene the state's bus operators and RTOs; controls the political narrative around the ongoing transport revival, which CFI could help shape to foreground safety metrics rather than only connectivity/emissions metrics.
key_individuals.suggested_approach: Engage around the ongoing Passenger Transport Vision Summit / Mobility Vision 2030 process -- offer CFI as a technical partner on the safety-feature specifications for the new bus fleets and PPP contracts, which is already an open, receptive agenda item for him.
key_individuals.caveats: His public messaging currently foregrounds connectivity, electrification and PPP economics over safety; safety features are mentioned but not yet the headline framing, so CFI should expect to actively pitch the safety angle rather than assume it is already his primary lens.
key_individuals.priorities_and_interests: Inferred from his public statements and portfolio: his central political project is reviving Madhya Pradesh's long-dormant state bus service (a 21-year gap) as a visible delivery success for the Yadav government, with electrification, PPP investment and rural connectivity as the headline metrics; embedding road-safety asks inside this existing bus-revival agenda (e.g. as a specification for the PPP contracts) is more likely to succeed than a separate safety-only pitch.

key_individuals.name: Rakesh Singh
key_individuals.role: Cabinet Minister for Public Works Department (PWD), Government of Madhya Pradesh (BJP); in office since 25 December 2023.
key_individuals.priority: Controls the roughly 80,000 km PWD road network (state highways, major and other district roads) -- a core CFI engagement target for engineering-side road safety (bypasses, signage, blackspot rectification).
key_individuals.influence: High -- ministerial head of the department that builds and maintains the majority of the state's non-national-highway road network and oversees a large engineering cadre.
key_individuals.road_safety_relevance: Moderate -- department framing under him emphasises quality/technology (AI-based pothole detection, green building standards) and some safety-adjacent bypass projects, but he has not made a headline road-safety policy statement.

track_record.text: At a PWD/MP Building Development Corporation engineers' capacity-building workshop where CM Yadav launched the Project Management System (PMS) 2.0 portal, highlighted the department's focus on green building standards (mandatory environmental compliance for projects over Rs 10 crore) and announced 293 new engineering positions approved.

citation.label: CM Mohan Yadav Inaugurates PWD Engineers' Workshop, Launches PMS Portal (tier-4, starsamachar.com, 12 Feb 2026)

track_record.confidence: Single tier-4 source; direct paraphrase of statements attributed to the PWD Minister, not independently corroborated elsewhere in this research.

key_individuals.frequency_of_engagement: Periodic -- appears at departmental capacity-building and infrastructure events roughly every few months; road-safety framing is present only indirectly (quality/technology emphasis) rather than as an explicit safety campaign.
key_individuals.background: Former seven-term Lok Sabha MP for Jabalpur (2004-2023) and ex-state BJP president; now MLA from Jabalpur West and PWD Minister since December 2023.
key_individuals.value_to_crashfree: Can direct PWD's engineering wings to prioritise blackspot rectification, mandate safety audits on new PWD works, and respond to the CAG's 2025 performance-audit findings (technical-sanction gaps, outdated maintenance yardsticks) with reforms that also improve safety outcomes.

focus_areas.name: Crash Compensation (Hit-and-Run Scheme)
focus_areas.relevance: Madhya Pradesh's hit-and-run problem is not a marginal concern within Crashfree India's national portfolio -- it is the largest single state-level manifestation of the exact implementation gap the program exists to close. MoRTH's own Lok Sabha data (April 2026) shows Madhya Pradesh recorded 11,550 (2020), 9,690 (2021), 12,250 (2022), 14,093 (2023) and 12,453 (2024, provisional) hit-and-run accidents -- in every year shown, more than double the next-highest state, making MP the undisputed epicentre of India's hit-and-run crisis. Yet claims uptake mirrors, and in the earliest years falls well below, the roughly 12% national uptake rate CFI's own brief cites: only 1 claim was registered in 2022-23 against roughly 12,000 accidents that year, rising to 73 in 2023-24, 231 in 2024-25, and 929 in the still-incomplete 2025-26 year (as of 28 Feb 2026). Cumulatively, that is only 1,234 claims registered against more than 50,000 hit-and-run accidents recorded across 2020-2024 -- an uptake rate under 3%, well below the already-dismal ~12% national average CFI's brief cites. Of registered claims, less than half have historically converted to payment (592 of 1,234 cumulative, per Free Press Journal reporting). This combination -- the country's highest hit-and-run volume paired with an uptake rate below the national average -- arguably makes MP a stronger candidate for a second Crashfree India pilot than the comparator geographies (Gurugram, Bihar, Delhi) named in CFI's own brief, none of which carry MP's accident volume. CFI's Jaipur pilot methodology -- mapping the claim journey from police to Claims Enquiry Officer to Claims Settlement Commissioner to the General Insurance Council, and building SOPs/portals/WhatsApp journeys -- addresses precisely the documentation-gap failure mode (90% of stalled claims nationally) that MP's own officials now publicly acknowledge.
focus_areas.progress: The most concrete recent development is administrative rather than CFI-driven: Madhya Pradesh's hit-and-run compensation portal went live in January 2026, and a State Road Safety Council member, K. Gautam, was quoted by Free Press Journal in April 2026 conceding the scheme 'had not been properly implemented in the state' -- an unusually candid admission that helps explain the historically negligible claims volume. The subsequent jump to 929 registered claims in 2025-26 (as of 28 Feb 2026), against just 231 in all of 2024-25, is consistent with a portal-driven uptick in filings, though it is genuinely unclear from available reporting whether this refers to a dedicated MP state portal or MP-specific uptake of the national e-Jagriti/General Insurance Council portal introduced under the March 2026 central amendment scheme -- an ambiguity this research could not resolve. Officials cited by Free Press Journal (April 2026) named lack of public awareness, documentation delays, and poor coordination between police, hospitals, and administrative authorities as the primary obstacles -- the same failure modes CFI's Jaipur pilot is designed around. Separately, the Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety (SCCoRS) reviewed Madhya Pradesh's district-level road-safety machinery in Jabalpur (reported August 2026), pushing a '4 Es' framework (engineering, enforcement, emergency care, education) and recommending expansion of the state's 'Zero Fatality District' programme to Indore, Bhopal and Ujjain -- general road-safety administrative activity, though not specifically targeted at hit-and-run claims processing. No evidence was found of MP-specific SOP documents, a dedicated claims dashboard, or a DRSC review cadence for hit-and-run claims comparable to CFI's Jaipur build-out; the state's visible response so far looks like the bare national portal rollout rather than a bespoke process fix.
focus_areas.policy_willpower: Signals are mixed. Positively, Madhya Pradesh's cabinet under CM Dr. Mohan Yadav approved a state-level 'Rahveer Yojana' on 27 May 2025 -- layered on top of the central Rah-Veer Good Samaritan scheme -- offering ₹25,000 to anyone who transports an accident victim to a primary health centre, explicitly citing MP's position among India's top five states for road fatalities (58,580 deaths, 2018-2022) and PM Modi's Mann Ki Baat remarks as motivation. This is a genuine, dated instance of executive willpower on accident-response incentives. The state also shows continuing DRSC/SCCoRS review activity (Jabalpur, August 2026) and a black-spot rectification programme (481 to 450 black spots, 2024-2025, per state PTRI data) attributed to sustained interdepartmental effort (NHAI, MPRDC, PWD, UADD, MPRRDA). However, none of this activity is specifically about hit-and-run claims processing, and the Rah-Veer scheme's own cumulative award count in MP is just 54 (as of 12 Feb 2026) -- strikingly small relative to MP's accident volume, suggesting the incentive has not meaningfully changed bystander behaviour or that awareness of it remains low. On the Saurabh Sharma transport-department corruption scandal (RTO check-post extortion, ₹500-700 crore, broke Dec 2024, arrest Jan 2025, investigating Lokayukta DG transferred March 2025): no source found in this research directly ties that scandal to hit-and-run claim administration -- it concerned vehicle/transporter check-post bribery, a different function within the same Transport Department. It is a reasonable but unverified inference that the scandal strained Transport Department credibility and bandwidth broadly; any causal link to hit-and-run implementation specifically should be treated as speculative, absent direct reporting.
focus_areas.cfi_engagement: No evidence found that Crashfree India is currently active in Madhya Pradesh on this program; the organisation's own materials name Jaipur (Rajasthan) as its sole pilot and cite Gurugram, Bihar, and Delhi as comparators, with Madhya Pradesh absent from all Crashfree India crash-compensation content reviewed (crashfreeindia.org/our-work/crash-claim-compensation).

focus_areas.name: Gig Rider Safety
focus_areas.relevance: Madhya Pradesh is independently reported as the third-most accident-prone state in India (World Bank, July 2024 feature, citing roughly 12,000 road deaths in 2019), and two-wheelers -- the vehicle class gig delivery and bike-taxi workers almost exclusively use -- already account nationally for nearly half of India's road fatalities, per CFI's own brief. Indore and Bhopal are both large, fast-growing metro-tier cities with the dense urban delivery footprints (food delivery, quick-commerce, ride-hailing) that make gig-rider exposure a measurable, growing local problem, consistent with the national trend of a gig workforce projected to exceed 23 million by 2030. An academic study chapter titled "Behavioral Analysis and Risk Segmentation of Two-Wheeler Delivery Riders: A Data-Driven Exploratory Study in Urban India" (Springer Nature) appears, based on available search-result summaries, to examine roughly 300 two-wheeler delivery riders specifically in Bhopal, covering risky riding behaviour, work-related stress, environmental factors and accidents -- categories that closely mirror the 'delivery pressure, working conditions, and road environment' framing of CFI's own 300+-rider national survey. This is a notable independent signal that Madhya Pradesh already has a measurable, research-documented gig-rider safety problem, even though CFI's own programme has not yet named any state-specific pilot. The full text of this study sits behind a login wall and could not be accessed in this research, so its findings should be treated as a promising lead rather than a confirmed data point.
focus_areas.progress: Crashfree India's own Gig Rider Safety programme remains, by its own account, national and thematic in scope: it launched in February 2026, is built on interviews conducted November 2025-January 2026, and has since surveyed 300+ two-wheeler gig riders nationally, with full findings due mid-October 2026 -- no state-specific pilot has been named anywhere in CFI's public materials reviewed (homepage, gig-rider-safety page). Independently, the Bhopal-focused academic study referenced above suggests some research infrastructure and researcher interest already exists locally around delivery-rider risk in Madhya Pradesh, which is a resource CFI could plausibly draw on once its own state-selection process begins, but there is no evidence CFI and this academic effort are connected. The gap between a nationally-scoped CFI survey (300+ riders, findings due mid-October 2026) and a seemingly disconnected academic dataset already covering roughly 300 Bhopal riders is itself a finding: it suggests Madhya Pradesh could readily supply comparable data to CFI's national workstream, but nothing indicates the two efforts have been connected as of this research (26 September 2026). No MP state-government programme, welfare board, or gig-worker safety initiative specific to two-wheeler delivery workers was found. No evidence was found of any MP city (Indore, Bhopal, Gwalior, Jabalpur) piloting gig-rider-specific interventions, welfare boards, delivery-time regulation, or platform-safety audits.
focus_areas.policy_willpower: No Madhya Pradesh-specific policy willpower signal was found on gig/two-wheeler delivery-rider safety as a distinct category. The state's visible road-safety political energy -- CM Mohan Yadav's cabinet approving the Rahveer Yojana (May 2025), the 2026-27 state budget's roads/bridges allocations (₹900 crore for bridge and culvert repair), and ring-road projects across Bhopal, Indore, Jabalpur, Gwalior and Ujjain -- is about general infrastructure and emergency response, not gig-worker-specific labour or road conditions. Nationally, some regulatory pressure exists (a broader 'gig workers law' conversation is underway per business/policy commentary reviewed), but none of this was found to have a Madhya Pradesh-specific implementing mechanism (no state gig-worker welfare board, no state transport-department rider-safety directive) in the sources reviewed. Given the state government has shown willingness to legislate/administer quickly on road safety generally when politically salient (the Rahveer Yojana was approved by cabinet in a single sitting, tied explicitly to a PM Mann Ki Baat mention), the absence of any comparable MP gig-rider signal likely reflects the issue's lower political salience relative to headline hit-and-run and black-spot numbers, rather than administrative incapacity. This is an honest gap: no MP-specific gig-rider policy willpower signal, positive or negative, was found in this research.
focus_areas.cfi_engagement: Crashfree India's Gig Rider Safety work is entirely national/thematic at this stage (launched Feb 2026, national rider survey, findings due mid-October 2026); no Madhya Pradesh-specific engagement, pilot, or partnership was found or claimed anywhere in Crashfree India's own materials.

focus_areas.name: Project Rakshak
focus_areas.relevance: Unlike Crashfree India's other three focus programs, Project Rakshak already has a confirmed, on-the-ground presence in Madhya Pradesh: Crashfree India's own Project Rakshak work-map dashboard lists three audited crash-prone corridors in Indore -- Teen Imli Square, Tejaji Nagar Junction, and Rau Gol Square -- among the 31 sites audited across 18 cities in Cohort 1 (2025). This makes Madhya Pradesh, via Indore, one of the program's founding-cohort geographies, not merely a hypothetical expansion target. The choice of Indore fits the program's model well: Indore hosts IIT Indore, whose 'Team Visioneers' was named one of Cohort 1's five top-performing teams on Crashfree India's own program page, and Indore already carries substantial state-government road-safety machinery to plug into -- it was one of three districts (with Dhar and Datia) in a 2023-2024 World Bank-backed Community Participatory Road Safety Program that reported a 70% accident reduction in pilot corridors, and the Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety recommended in August 2026 that the state's 'Zero Fatality District' programme be extended to cover Indore directly. All three named corridor intersections are real, well-known high-traffic Indore junctions, consistent with the 'high-risk corridor' targeting Project Rakshak's model describes. This is the single strongest, most concrete Crashfree India engagement point found anywhere in this research across all four MP focus areas, and should be treated as a genuine existing outreach asset rather than a gap to fill.
focus_areas.progress: Crashfree India's own Project Rakshak dashboard (crashfreeindia.org/rakshak/dashboard) confirms Indore, Madhya Pradesh as one of Cohort 1's 18 covered cities, with three specific audited locations: Teen Imli Square, Tejaji Nagar Junction, and Rau Gol Square. These sit within Cohort 1's overall reported totals of 31 audited sites, 23+ government approvals secured, and a programme-wide claimed '30% crash reduction' outcome metric (all per the dashboard; the 30% figure could not be independently broken out for Indore specifically, nor verified against an outside source). IIT Indore's 'Team Visioneers' was separately named among Cohort 1's five headline 'top-performing teams' on the main Project Rakshak page, and given IIT Indore's Indore location, it is highly likely (though not explicitly stated together in the page text extracted) that this team was responsible for the Indore corridor audits. What could not be confirmed: which specific government body (Indore Municipal Corporation, Indore Traffic Police, PWD, or Indore Smart City Ltd) granted the approvals attributed to the Indore sites, what engineering fixes were proposed for each of the three junctions, or whether any physical intervention has actually been implemented at Teen Imli Square, Tejaji Nagar, or Rau Gol Square as of September 2026. No independent (non-CFI) press coverage of this Indore work was found in this research, so all detail currently rests on Crashfree India's own dashboard and program page. It is also unconfirmed whether Madhya Pradesh/Indore continues into Cohort 2 (2026, 95 teams/34 cities) -- the full Cohort 2 city list is not separately published anywhere reviewed.
focus_areas.policy_willpower: Madhya Pradesh's state government has demonstrated real, multi-year administrative appetite for exactly the corridor-level, multi-agency audit-and-fix model Project Rakshak uses, which likely helps explain why Indore was a receptive host city: the state's black-spot rectification programme cut identified black spots from 481 to 450 (2024-2025), completed 169 long-term rectification works by July 2026, and draws on a standing multi-agency coalition (NHAI, MPRDC, PWD-NH, PWD-B&R, UADD, MPRRDA) that could plausibly overlap with the machinery that granted Project Rakshak's Indore-site approvals. The Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety's Jabalpur review (August 2026) explicitly recommended extending the state's 'Zero Fatality District' programme to Indore, Bhopal and Ujjain -- showing continuing state-level appetite to formalize corridor-level safety work in exactly these cities. This is a genuinely positive willpower signal: Madhya Pradesh already runs comparable audit-to-fix civic infrastructure at scale, independent of Crashfree India, which both plausibly explains Project Rakshak's traction in Indore and suggests real headroom for CFI to expand within the state (e.g., to Bhopal, which the SC Committee separately flagged) if it chooses to. No direct quote, press release, or MoU from an Indore civic authority naming Crashfree India or Project Rakshak specifically was found, so the causal link between state appetite and CFI's approvals should be read as circumstantial rather than confirmed; the approvals could equally have come through a channel unconnected to the state's broader Zero Fatality/black-spot programmes.
focus_areas.cfi_engagement: Confirmed and positive: Crashfree India's own Project Rakshak dashboard lists Indore, Madhya Pradesh as one of Cohort 1's 18 covered cities, with three audited corridors (Teen Imli Square, Tejaji Nagar Junction, Rau Gol Square), and IIT Indore's 'Team Visioneers' is named among the cohort's five top-performing teams -- making this the only one of Crashfree India's four focus programs with a clearly confirmed, named Madhya Pradesh presence.

focus_areas.name: SATARK (ANPR Enforcement Technology)
focus_areas.relevance: SATARK's model -- ANPR plate-scanning matched in real time against compliance/challan records, with an alert routed to on-ground police for priority violations -- is a natural conceptual fit for a state with Madhya Pradesh's enforcement volume: Jabalpur district alone issued over 1.09 lakh challans in 2025 and a further 28,555 by March 2026 under intensified DRSC-driven enforcement, and the state already runs a mature, statewide e-challan system (echallan.mponline.gov.in) covering Bhopal, Indore, Gwalior and Jabalpur. Where SATARK would add value over MP's existing e-challan system is its real-time officer-alert and public 'AI Challan Billboard' layer -- flagging a violation at the moment a flagged vehicle passes a camera, rather than mailing a challan after the fact -- a materially different enforcement posture from MP's current after-the-fact model. Given MP's exceptionally high hit-and-run volume, a real-time enforcement-alert layer is conceptually attractive (a plate scan cannot identify a hit-and-run perpetrator whose plate was never captured at the scene, but it can flag drivers with existing violation histories moving through high-risk corridors), though it is not a direct fix for hit-and-run identification itself, which depends on witness testimony or scene-adjacent CCTV rather than routine ANPR checkpoints.
focus_areas.progress: Madhya Pradesh's own ANPR/e-challan infrastructure is limited to the standard automated-detection-and-mail-a-challan model already in wide use across Indian states, run through the state's official portal (echallan.mponline.gov.in) covering Bhopal, Indore, Gwalior and Jabalpur; no evidence was found of any Madhya Pradesh deployment with SATARK's specific real-time-alert-to-officer or public compliance-billboard features. No news coverage, government notification, or CFI/Cars24 announcement was found of any SATARK installation, pilot, or planned expansion into any Madhya Pradesh city. This is consistent with Crashfree India's own brief, which places SATARK as live only in Bengaluru, Gurugram, and Jaipur, with four more installations (Pune, Rajkot, Gandhinagar, Thiruvananthapuram) underway -- none in Madhya Pradesh, and nothing in CFI's own published materials suggests MP is under consideration next. Madhya Pradesh's broader digitization and infrastructure push under CM Mohan Yadav has focused on ring-road and highway construction (Bhopal, Indore, Jabalpur, Gwalior, Ujjain) rather than enforcement technology specifically, per state budget and infrastructure reporting reviewed for this research, suggesting SATARK-style enforcement tech is not currently a visible state government priority relative to physical road-building. No MP-specific enforcement-technology vendor announcement, state IT-department tender, or Home Department circular referencing ANPR-based real-time alerting was located.
focus_areas.policy_willpower: No policy-willpower signal specific to ANPR/AI-based real-time enforcement technology was found for Madhya Pradesh. The state's demonstrated technology appetite is centred on the existing statewide e-challan portal and general digitization of traffic-fine payment/status-checking, not on next-generation real-time alerting. The state's broader road-safety political energy in 2025-26 -- the Rahveer Yojana, black-spot rectification, Zero Fatality District expansion, SCCoRS district reviews -- has been engineering- and emergency-response-focused rather than enforcement-technology-focused. Given that SATARK is a Cars24-built technology (Cars24 also incubated Crashfree India itself), any MP deployment would likely require either a direct CFI/Cars24-state MoU (as apparently exists in Bengaluru, Gurugram, and Jaipur) or an independent state procurement decision; no signal of either was found. No mention of SATARK, Cars24's ANPR technology, or a comparable AI-challan-billboard concept was found in any Madhya Pradesh Assembly proceeding, state budget document, or Home/Transport Department press statement reviewed. This should be read as an honest absence of evidence rather than confirmation that MP has considered and rejected SATARK-style technology -- the research found no discussion of the technology in MP policy circles at all, positive or negative.
focus_areas.cfi_engagement: SATARK is not live or planned in Madhya Pradesh; Crashfree India's own brief lists Bengaluru, Gurugram, and Jaipur as live and Pune, Rajkot, Gandhinagar, and Thiruvananthapuram as underway, with no Madhya Pradesh city named in any tier, and no independent research found any indication this is under consideration.

assam.political_context: Assam held Legislative Assembly elections in 2026, and Himanta Biswa Sarma (BJP) was returned for a second term as Chief Minister, with the Second Sarma ministry sworn in on 12 May 2026 (initial CM-plus-four ceremony) followed by a full cabinet expansion to 17 ministers (14 BJP, 2 AGP, 1 BPF) confirmed by 16 June 2026. Assam's Second Sarma ministry has NO Deputy Chief Minister -- a genuine structural feature (re-checked this pass; no source names one), unlike Bihar or several other states in this document series, meaning there is no 'number two' political figure to route outreach through. CM Sarma personally holds an unusually concentrated set of portfolios directly relevant to road safety: Home (except Prisons, Home Guards), Personnel, Public Works (Buildings & National Highways), Public Works (Roads), and -- per the state's own cabinet-list sources -- Medical Education & Research, though a later (16 June 2026) independent tabulation instead lists Medical Education & Research under Health Minister Ashok Singhal; this discrepancy is unresolved and flagged. This gives one office simultaneous control of enforcement (Home/Police), road engineering (both PWD wings), and the state's Road Safety Council chairmanship (ex officio, by virtue of being CM). Other road-safety-relevant portfolios: Transport & Welfare of Bodoland (Charan Boro, BPF), Health & Family Welfare (Ashok Singhal, BJP, also ex officio GMDA Chairperson), Finance, Environment & Forest, Mines & Minerals (Jayanta Mallabaruah, BJP, since 5 June 2026 -- Finance is the ex officio-adjacent portfolio relevant to the Assam Road Safety Fund's cess and grant flows, though the Fund Management Committee itself is chaired by the Chief Secretary, not the Finance Minister), Revenue & Disaster Management (Keshab Mahanta, AGP), and Panchayat & Rural Development / Implementation of Assam Accord / Excise / Border Protection & Development (Atul Bora, AGP). Dr. Ravi Kota, IAS (1993 batch) is Chief Secretary, in the post since 17 January 2024 with his tenure formally extended by six months beyond superannuation, from 1 May 2026 to 31 October 2026 -- meaning a Chief Secretary transition is likely within weeks of this research date (25 September 2026) and any CFI relationship-building with his office should anticipate a successor. Kota has a genuine, dated road-safety track record: on 29 April 2026 he chaired a statewide road-safety review (Q1 2026 data: 4,219 accidents, 1,008 fatalities, nine districts accounting for ~50% of fatalities), directed NHAI/NHIDCL/PWD suo motu action on black spots, and explicitly urged districts to draw on Road Safety Fund money and partner with NGOs on signage -- a direct, documented opening for Crashfree India. Harmeet Singh, IPS (1992-batch, Assam-Meghalaya cadre) remains DGP, re-confirmed current by an official Assam Police directory dated 19 August 2026 (the most current dated primary source located this pass, superseding the January/March 2026 snapshots used previously). The same 19 August 2026 directory resolves a prior flag with strong, current, official corroboration: Dr. P.S. Mahanta, IPS (2007-batch, promotee) holds three concurrent titles -- Commissioner of Police, Guwahati; IGP (Traffic & Road Safety), Assam; and Chief of the State Task Force -- and Jayanta Sarathi Borah, APS is confirmed as DCP (Traffic), Guwahati Commissionerate. A separate IGP (BTAD), Bijoy Giri Kuligam, IPS, heads policing specifically in the Bodoland Territorial Area Districts. This pass also confirms a genuinely current (as of 25 September 2026), still-pending Gauhati High Court road-safety PIL -- Gaurav Dey vs. The State of Assam & 7 Ors, PIL/31/2026 -- filed by a Guwahati law student challenging the absence of safety regulation (blind-spot mitigation, 360-degree cameras, speed limiters, operating-hours restrictions) for dumper/tipper trucks, naming the Transport Department, police authorities, the Regional Transport Officer, MoRTH, and vehicle manufacturers Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland as respondents; the case was last heard 15 September 2026 and adjourned to 16 November 2026. This resolves the prior 'no current PIL found' gap and gives Crashfree India both a live litigation to track and a genuine, documented individual road-safety champion (Gaurav Dey) outside government. A second, independent documented road-safety champion was found: Bhupen Borah, BJP MLA for Bihpuria, publicly urged the state government and police (3 June 2026) to seize motorcycles for a month and impose age-based speed restrictions on young riders after fatal helmetless-riding accidents in his constituency -- he should not be confused with the differently-spelled Congress leader/former APCC president of a similar name, a distinction worth flagging for CFI staff. Devajit (Lon) Saikia was re-appointed Advocate General of Assam for a second five-year term on 13 May 2026 (having resigned 6 May 2026 per constitutional convention when the outgoing government's term ended) -- relevant given his office's institutional role in defending the state in PIL/31/2026 and any future road/bridge litigation. The Leader of the Opposition in the Assam Legislative Assembly is Wazed Ali Choudhury (INC), who assumed the position on 27 May 2026 (Deputy Leader: Joy Prakash Das, INC). A genuinely distinct institutional wrinkle this pass investigated in depth, per the client's specific request: the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR/BTC) runs its own parallel road-governance structure for its constituent districts (Kokrajhar, Chirang, Baksa, Udalguri, Tamulpur), separate from the state PWRD/Transport Department chain of command that governs the rest of Assam. Following BTC's own September 2025 council election (won outright by the Bodoland People's Front, 28 of 40 seats) and a 28 November 2025 portfolio reallocation, BTC Chief Executive Member Hagrama Mohilary (BPF) personally holds PWD, Panchayat & Rural Development, and Finance within BTC (mirroring, at the sub-state level, the same pattern of one office concentrating road-engineering and fiscal control seen with CM Sarma at the state level), while BTC Executive Member Mritunjoy Narzary holds the Transport portfolio within BTC. Notably, Charan Boro -- the state's own Transport Minister -- and Hagrama Mohilary belong to the same party (BPF), which currently controls both the state Transport portfolio and the entirety of BTC's executive, a genuine and useful political alignment for any Crashfree India engagement strategy that needs to work across the BTAD boundary. India's Seventh Schedule splits road-related subjects across the Union and State Lists (roads, transport and police sit substantially on the State List, with the Union retaining National Highways, the Motor Vehicles Act framework, and centrally sponsored schemes like PMGSY), so Assam's state government -- and, within BTAD specifically, the BTC executive -- are the primary points of leverage for nearly all road-safety interventions Crashfree India will pursue.

governance_bodies.decision_making_power: Because PWRD (not a separate rural department) holds both arterial and rural road engineering authority statewide, and because the CM holds this portfolio personally, Assam has an unusually centralised road-engineering decision structure compared with every other state in this document series. governance_bodies.data_role: Runs both the core PMGSY rural-connectivity programme and the dedicated PMGSY Maintenance Branch (eMARG) for periodic renewal of already-built PMGSY roads. Has identified 16 black spots on State Highways and Major District Roads following MoRTH guidelines, with mitigation measures including retro-reflective road signs, road markings, rumble strips and speed breakers.

governance_bodies.name: Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC) / Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR) — PWD & road authority under the Sixth Schedule
governance_bodies.mandate: BTC is a Sixth-Schedule autonomous self-governing body for the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTAD), covering the districts of Kokrajhar, Chirang, Baksa and Udalguri, created by the 10 February 2003 Memorandum of Settlement among the Government of India, Government of Assam and the Bodo Liberation Tigers, and given constitutional protection under the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution. "PWD" is listed as item 5 of 40 subjects the 2003 accord specifies as being "entrusted to BTC by [the] Assam Government," alongside Transport (item 29) and Panchayat and Rural Development (item 12) as separate, also-transferred subjects. THIS SPECIFIC ATTRIBUTION RESTS ON THE PRIMARY ACCORD TEXT AS ARCHIVED BY THE UN PEACEMAKER TREATY DATABASE, NOT ON AN ASSAM GAZETTE OR PIB COPY: mha.gov.in and pib.gov.in pages on the Bodo Accord returned access errors (403) when checked directly in this pass, and this is flagged as a sourcing limitation rather than resolved.
governance_bodies.roads_owned: Nominally ambiguous, and this is the key structural finding for Crashfree India's outreach purposes: although "PWD" appears on the accord's list of subjects transferred to BTC, state PWRD's own official website confirms it continues to operate a full zonal engineering structure INSIDE the BTAD area — a dedicated "BTC Zone" (HQ Kokrajhar) under its own Additional Chief Engineer, with a "Kokrajhar (R&B) Circle" beneath it — and Chirang district's own government portal separately confirms a state-department "PWD (R&B) Division, Chirang," established 2008, running PMGSY/CMGSY/NESIDS-funded works from its headquarters at Kajolgaon, with no reference on that page to any separate BTC PWD authority. This indicates that, in practice, the Government of Assam's own PWRD/PWD(B&NH) continues to directly plan, execute and maintain State Highways, Major District Roads and PMGSY rural roads inside BTAD through its normal statewide zonal hierarchy, rather than having handed that engineering function wholesale to BTC. Separately, BTC does maintain its own PWD department (headquartered at the BTC Secretariat, Kokrajhar, per publicly listed BTC tender notices for road works), which appears to function alongside — not in place of — the state's Kokrajhar-zone PWRD/PWD offices, most plausibly for roads and works that fall outside the state's own road classification (SH/MDR/PMGSY) or for BTC's own locally-initiated development-plan works funded from its population-ratio-based grants-in-aid from the State Government.
governance_bodies.hierarchy: BTC has an Executive Council of up to 12 Executive Members (a Chief and Deputy Chief with Cabinet-Minister-equivalent status for protocol purposes in the BTC area), with executive functions exercised through a Principal Secretary (an officer not below Commissioner/Secretary rank in the Government of Assam) and, for delegated subjects such as PWD, a senior departmental officer who may be designated "Director of BTC" for that department. This BTC-side hierarchy sits alongside, not beneath, the state PWRD's own BTC Zone/Kokrajhar Circle chain of command described above.
governance_bodies.subordinate_bodies: BTC's own PWD Department (Kokrajhar); separately, and administratively distinct, the state PWRD's BTC Zone (Additional Chief Engineer, HQ Kokrajhar) and Kokrajhar (R&B) Circle, and the state PWD (R&B) Division, Chirang.
governance_bodies.decision_making_power: For Crashfree India's outreach purposes, the practical implication is that a road-safety problem inside the four BTAD districts cannot be assumed to fall under BTC's authority merely because "PWD" is nominally a nominally BTC-devolved subject: State Highways, Major District Roads and PMGSY roads within BTAD very plausibly remain under the state PWRD's own BTC-Zone/Kokrajhar-Circle chain (the same chain that reports to the Chief Engineer, PWD (Roads) and ultimately the CM as Minister, PWD (Roads)), while BTC's own PWD Department handles a separate, narrower set of works. Confirming which authority owns a specific road inside BTAD requires a direct, road-specific check before outreach — flagged explicitly as a research gap below.

governance_bodies.performance_issues: Not established from the sources reviewed; the general BTC road-infrastructure statistics available (2,680 gravelled roads, 2,650 blacktopped roads completed, and NH work in progress, per council-cited 2015–16-vintage figures) are now over a decade stale and are not included here as current data.

governance_bodies.meeting_frequency: No confirmed meeting under the Council's specific name since 2016; the State Road Safety Authority Bill, 2017 has NOT been enacted — it remained "under circulation for views and comments of stake holding Departments" as of the most recent department statement reviewed, placing Assam in the executive-rules governance-model category (alongside Bihar/Jharkhand) rather than a dedicated-statutory-Authority model (e.g. Karnataka's KSRSA).

key_individuals.name: Himanta Biswa Sarma
key_individuals.role: Chief Minister of Assam since 2021, re-elected for a second term with the ministry sworn in 12 May 2026; personally holds Home (except Prisons/Home Guards), Personnel, PWD (Buildings & NH), PWD (Roads); ex officio Chair, Assam Road Safety Council.
key_individuals.priority: Reserve a CM-level ask for a fully-formed, cross-department initiative -- not a first point of contact.
key_individuals.influence: Uniquely among the states in this document series, one person simultaneously chairs the state's road-safety council, controls its two largest road-engineering departments, and controls its police/enforcement chain.
key_individuals.road_safety_relevance: No personal, in-his-own-words road-safety advocacy record was found in this pass (distinct from his Chief Secretary's documented April 2026 road-safety review, which Sarma did not personally chair per the sources found), though he chairs the Assam Road Safety Council by virtue of office.

key_individuals.background: Political leadership -- ruling party (BJP); previously held Health & Finance portfolios before becoming CM in 2021.
key_individuals.value_to_crashfree: Highest-leverage relationship in Assam given his simultaneous control of the Road Safety Council chairmanship, road engineering, and enforcement -- but precisely because of that concentration, a poorly-prepared CM-level ask has nowhere else to be redirected if it lands badly.
key_individuals.suggested_approach: Not a first point of contact. Build documented engagement with the Transport Minister, the Chief Secretary's office (which has already run a real 2026 road-safety review CFI can reference directly), and the Commissioner of Transport first; reserve a CM-level ask for a fully-formed, cross-department initiative.
key_individuals.caveats: Personal road-safety advocacy record not established; the Medical Education & Research portfolio attribution conflicts between sources (see flags) and should be confirmed before referencing it in outreach.
key_individuals.priorities_and_interests: Sarma's public agenda in 2026 has centred on consolidating a second-term BJP-led coalition (BJP+AGP+BPF) after the Assam election, continuing his long-running emphasis on the Clean/Assam Accord-implementation and anti-illegal-immigration planks that have defined his first term, and positioning himself as a national BJP strategist beyond Assam. His concentration of Home, both PWD wings, and Personnel in his own hands is consistent with a governance style built on direct, centralised control rather than delegation, which cuts both ways for road safety: it means the single most consequential road-safety decision-maker in the state is also the hardest to get dedicated time with, and any change he personally champions can move unusually fast because it does not require cross-ministerial coordination. Inference (not directly documented): given that he chairs the Road Safety Council only ex officio and no personal road-safety statement was found this pass, road safety is very likely a background administrative responsibility for him rather than an active personal priority, making his Chief Secretary and Transport Minister the more realistic near-term entry points.

assam.source_audit: This research pass (25 September 2026) built on Assam's existing dataset entry rather than starting from zero, and focused specifically on: (1) building a complete 15-stage x 3-category road_lifecycle table, which the existing dataset entirely lacked; (2) resolving the Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC) / road-authority structural question the task specifically asked to verify; and (3) removing disallowed-source citations (Wikipedia, and one X/Twitter citation for Mrityunjoy-108 fleet data) that were present in the prior pass's governance_bodies entries, replacing them with dated Indian mainstream-press or official government-website citations wherever a suitable replacement could be found and independently rendered. Where a suitable allowed-source replacement could NOT be independently rendered in this pass (Atul Bora's exact current portfolio; the precise BTC/PWD subject-transfer legal citation), this is disclosed explicitly in the affected entries and in research_gaps rather than silently carrying forward the old Wikipedia citation or fabricating a stronger one. Primary new findings in this pass, and their sourcing: (a) PWRD's detailed hierarchy (Secretary Debajit Das, Commissioner Sanjiv Shyam, three Chief Engineers, six geographic zones including a dedicated "BTC Zone") — sourced entirely to pwdroads.assam.gov.in's own current contact/offices pages; (b) the BTC/road-authority finding — sourced to pwdroads.assam.gov.in (confirming the state's own BTC Zone/Kokrajhar Circle) and chirang.assam.gov.in (confirming a state, not BTC, PWD division operating inside a BTAD district), both official .gov.in sources, with the historical/legal "PWD is one of 40 transferred subjects" background sourced with an explicit caveat to the primary 2003 accord text as archived by UN Peacemaker (not a Gazette/PIB copy, which this pass could not retrieve after genuine, documented attempts against mha.gov.in and pib.gov.in, both of which returned 403 errors); (c) Transport Commissioner Akash Deep, IAS — sourced to transport.assam.gov.in's own current homepage; (d) the tri-partite NHAI/NHIDCL/PWD(NH) road-safety coordination structure and Chief Secretary Dr. Ravi Kota's identity — sourced to a dated (29 April 2026) Sentinel Assam report of a Chief-Secretary-chaired road-safety review, which also supplied current Q1-2026 accident/fatality statistics and confirmed the PM RAHAT cashless-treatment scheme's operation in Assam; (e) updated Mrityunjoy-108 fleet figures (over 800 ambulances as of November 2024 per Sentinel Assam; over 700 before an 82-unit expansion as of February 2026 per Pratidin Time), replacing the prior pass's X/Twitter citation. This pass's WebSearch tool quota was exhausted partway through (a session-wide, not Assam-specific, limit), after which further verification relied on WebFetch against specific, already-identified or logically-inferred government and news URLs rather than fresh open searches; several residual gaps listed in research_gaps reflect that cutoff rather than a failed search. Multiple official Assam government domains (assam.gov.in, cmo.assam.gov.in, wptbc.assam.gov.in, bodoland.gov.in and its subdomains, prd.assam.gov.in, revenueassam.nic.in, eparlib.sansad.in, pib.gov.in, mha.gov.in) returned 403/404/500/503 errors or DNS failures when checked directly in this pass; where a claim could only be supported by one of these inaccessible sources, it is either omitted or explicitly flagged as unresolved rather than asserted.

focus_areas.name: Crash Compensation (Hit-and-Run Scheme)
focus_areas.relevance: Assam is a striking case study for exactly the implementation problem Crashfree India (CFI) targets nationally: a documentation-and-awareness gap rather than a policy gap. Government data (Lok Sabha, MoRTH, 02 Apr 2026) shows hit-and-run accidents in Assam falling steadily from 1,235 (2020) to 925 (2024, provisional) — one of the few states with a declining trend. Yet Hit-and-Run Compensation Scheme claims were essentially zero for two straight years (0/0 in both FY2022-23 and FY2023-24), rising only to 13 registered/5 paid in FY2024-25 and 16 registered/9 paid by 28 February 2026 in FY2025-26. Set against ~925-1,163 accidents a year, single-digit-to-low-teens claims imply an uptake rate far below even the ~12% national average CFI's brief cites, despite Assam's accident count moving in the right direction. This mismatch — falling crashes, flat-to-negligible claims — is precisely the 'stalled on documentation, not on policy' pattern CFI's Jaipur pilot was built to fix, and it is compounded by the state's Rah-Veer (Good Samaritan) scheme showing only 1 cumulative awardee as of 12 February 2026, the lowest of any state that reported any awardees, suggesting the whole post-crash citizen/claimant response chain (bystander intervention through to compensation) is thin in Assam relative to its accident load. For an outreach dashboard, Assam is a strong candidate for CFI's comparator/expansion thinking precisely because the gap between accidents and claims is unusually stark and well-documented via the two Lok Sabha answers, even though CFI's own materials do not currently name Assam in this program.
focus_areas.progress: On the ground, Assam's District Road Safety Committees (DRSCs) — constituted under Section 215(3) of the MV Act and chaired by Deputy/District Commissioners — meet regularly and are visibly active: 2025-2026 reporting documents sessions in Sonitpur (64 accidents, 8 fatal, tracked through August 2026), Morigaon, Kamrup (chaired by DC Deba Kumar Mishra, 28 Aug 2026), Biswanath (ordering fixes at the high-risk Lehugaon Junction, 13 Aug 2026) and a student-awareness drive at Dudhnoi College in Goalpara. However, every meeting write-up reviewed for this research focused on blackspot engineering, accident-count reviews, or general student road-safety awareness — none surfaced any DRSC agenda item on hit-and-run compensation scheme documentation, claims processing, or public awareness of the scheme specifically, suggesting the 2026 national amendment's push for DRSC-level review of the scheme (rolling up to the state) has not yet visibly reached Assam's district committees in public reporting. Separately, Assam's general Victim Compensation Scheme (2012), run through the State/District Legal Services Authorities and unrelated to the hit-and-run scheme specifically, promises payout within about two months of a verified claim, run offline via bank transfer — but its own guidance page makes no mention of hit-and-run cases or awareness outreach. A high-profile case — the 25 July 2026 hit-and-run death of 21-year-old Nalbari Polytechnic student and GMC employee Samiul Haque in Guwahati's Dakhingaon area, in which actress Nandini Kashyap was arrested — drew press scrutiny of Dispur Police for reportedly skipping an alcohol test and delaying notification to the Traffic Branch, illustrating exactly the kind of first-responder documentation friction that stalls claims later in the pipeline nationally.
focus_areas.policy_willpower: Assam's most visible recent road-safety signal at the top of government came on 22 September 2026, when Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma stated that PM-RAHAT and the Rah-Veer scheme would 'strengthen the first response to accidents,' framing timely post-crash assistance as central to road safety. This is a genuine, dated policy signal of willpower on emergency response, but as reported it did not reference the Hit-and-Run Compensation Scheme, set any claims or awareness targets, or announce budget lines for the scheme specifically — the willpower visible so far is aimed at the golden-hour/Good Samaritan layer, not the compensation-claims layer where Assam's own data shows the gap is widest. No Assam-specific legislative debate, CAG audit, or budget allocation targeting the hit-and-run scheme's documentation bottleneck was found in the sources reviewed. Combined with DRSCs' apparent silence on the scheme in available minutes, the overall picture is one of active state attention to road safety infrastructure and emergency response, but no yet-visible dedicated push on the hit-and-run claims process itself — an opening for outreach.
focus_areas.cfi_engagement: Assam is not named anywhere in Crashfree India's own Crash Compensation brief or on its programme page (crashfreeindia.org/our-work/crash-claim-compensation), which centers on the Jaipur, Rajasthan pilot and cites Gurugram, Bihar and Delhi as comparators; CFI's own site content mentions only Delhi by name and gives no Assam-specific data or activity.

focus_areas.name: Gig Rider Safety
focus_areas.relevance: Guwahati is Northeast India's largest gig-economy hub, with Swiggy, Zomato/Blinkit, Zepto and Rapido all operating fleets of two-wheeler delivery and ride riders in a city whose road network (narrow arterial roads like GS Road, frequent waterlogging, mixed traffic) mirrors the risk factors CFI's national brief describes: nearly half of India's road-crash fatalities are two-wheeler riders, and 73% of two-wheeler riders/pillions who died in 2023 nationally were not wearing helmets. India's gig workforce is projected by Crashfree India's own brief to exceed 23 million by 2030, and national reporting (Newslaundry, Nov 2025) frames the scale bluntly: roughly nine two-wheeler riders die every hour on Indian roads amid rising gig-delivery volumes and aggressive delivery-time pressure. None of the national studies, surveys or advocacy pieces reviewed broke out Assam or Guwahati-specific casualty or rider-behaviour data, so the relevance case for Assam currently rests on inference from national patterns plus Guwahati's confirmed presence as an active delivery market, not on state-specific evidence.
focus_areas.progress: Crashfree India's Gig Rider Safety programme is explicitly national and thematic at this stage: it began in February 2026 building on research and interviews conducted November 2025-January 2026 with delivery and bike-taxi workers, and CFI has since surveyed 300+ two-wheeler gig riders nationally, with full findings due to publish mid-October 2026; CFI's own programme page (crashfreeindia.org/our-work/gig-rider-safety) is still marked 'Coming Soon' and names no state pilot or city priority list, including no mention of Assam, Guwahati or Northeast India. Separately, India's Social Security Code (notified November 2025) placed gig workers nationally — Assam's included — under a framework intended to require aggregator contributions toward accident and health coverage, and national pressure from the Union Labour Ministry led major platforms (Swiggy, Zomato, Blinkit, Zepto) to walk back explicit '10-minute delivery' branding in early 2026 after safety concerns were flagged; these are national developments that would apply to Guwahati's riders by default, but no Assam-specific implementation notice, aggregator response, or state labour department action was found.
focus_areas.policy_willpower: No evidence was found of the Assam Transport Department, Assam Police, or Assam Labour Department issuing gig/delivery-rider-specific safety directives, running helmet-compliance drives targeted at delivery fleets, or engaging directly with platform aggregators on rider safety. This should be read as an information gap rather than confirmed inaction: gig-rider safety is a very recent and still under-covered beat even in national Indian media, and state-level coverage of it in Assam is essentially absent from the sources searched, so it is not possible to responsibly characterize Assam's institutional posture on this specific issue one way or the other.
focus_areas.cfi_engagement: Crashfree India's Gig Rider Safety work is national/thematic in scope with no state-specific pilot named anywhere in its public materials; Assam does not appear in the programme's research locations, survey base, or forthcoming (mid-October 2026) findings as described on CFI's own site.

focus_areas.name: Project Rakshak
focus_areas.relevance: Project Rakshak's audit-to-fix model — youth teams researching a corridor's crash history, engaging stakeholders, and proposing infrastructure fixes to civic authorities — is a natural fit for Guwahati, which already has documented high-risk corridors and an existing state government precedent for corridor-level safety engineering: Assam's PWD (Roads) department runs a 'Model Safe Corridor Demonstration Programme' (SCDP) with Traffic System Management covering roughly 23 km of Guwahati from Jalukbari to Khanapara via MG Road-AT Road-GS Road. Guwahati also hosts technical institutions (including IIT Guwahati and several engineering/architecture colleges) that would be plausible partners for Rakshak's youth track, similar to the IIT Indore, IIT Madras, IIT BHU and other technical-institute teams that featured among Cohort 1's top performers nationally.
focus_areas.progress: Cohort 1 (2025) of Project Rakshak, per Crashfree India's own programme page, ran 31 teams across 18 cities, assessed 120+ high-risk locations, conducted 900+ stakeholder surveys and secured 23+ government approvals; the page does not publish the full 18-city list and makes no mention of Assam or Guwahati among named participants or top-performing teams (which included School of Planning and Architecture Vijayawada, IIT Indore, IIT Madras, St. Xavier's College Mumbai, and IIT BHU). For the 2026 second edition — 3 tracks (youth/NGOs/auditors), a 5-month youth-track programme, 95 teams across 34 cities and 32 institutions, 136 colleges reached, and MoUs with NOSPlan and SIT Pune, with 15 more teams expected from Jaipur, Pune and Srinagar — no independent source (CFI's own site, LinkedIn posts, or general press) surfaced a Guwahati or Assam institution, team, or partnership announcement. Separately and independently of CFI, Assam's PWD Roads department's own Safe Corridor Demonstration Programme shows the state already has an appetite for corridor-level traffic-safety engineering in Guwahati, but this is a state government initiative with no found link to Crashfree India or Project Rakshak.
focus_areas.policy_willpower: No Assam state government statement, college MoU, or civic-body engagement referencing Project Rakshak specifically was found. The existence of Assam PWD's own Safe Corridor Demonstration Programme for a Guwahati corridor suggests some institutional appetite for structured corridor-safety work that a Rakshak-style youth partnership could plug into, but this is inference, not a documented signal of willpower toward CFI's programme itself.
focus_areas.cfi_engagement: Assam/Guwahati does not appear in Project Rakshak's Cohort 1 outputs or in the publicly announced components of the 2026 second edition (the MoUs, named additional cities, and named institutions); no confirmation could be found either way on whether Guwahati is among the edition's 34 cities, since the full city list is not published.

focus_areas.name: SATARK (ANPR Enforcement Technology)
focus_areas.relevance: SATARK's model — ANPR-based automated enforcement live in Bengaluru, Gurugram and Jaipur, with four more cities underway (Pune, Rajkot, Gandhinagar, Thiruvananthapuram) — is relevant to Assam because Guwahati faces the same underlying enforcement-capacity problem SATARK targets: manual traffic policing struggling to keep pace with violations and hit-and-run incidents (as illustrated by the Nandini Kashyap case, where a documentation/procedural lapse by police was itself the story). Assam is not named as a current or planned SATARK location, but the state is independently building large-scale, ANPR-capable camera infrastructure through a separate channel, which matters for understanding whether Assam needs a SATARK-style partnership or already has adjacent technology in progress.
focus_areas.progress: Guwahati Smart City Limited (GSCL) is executing a roughly ₹220 crore citywide CCTV surveillance project explicitly specified (per GSCL's own tender documentation) to include 'Fixed Box, PTZ, and ANPR cameras' alongside Emergency Call Boxes, a Public Announcement System, environmental sensors and Visual Message Display systems, framed primarily around women/child/elderly public safety and traffic management. As reported by Sentinel Assam in June 2025, the project had reached roughly 50% completion, with about 100 cameras operational and cantilever poles erected at 650 of a planned 2,000+ camera locations (surveys done at 800+ sites), officials at the time projecting substantive completion by around September 2025; the system is designed to feed an Integrated Command and Control Centre at the Commissioner of Police's office in Khanapara, coordinated across GSCL, Assam Power Distribution Corporation, Guwahati Municipal Corporation and Guwahati Jal Board. No source reviewed post-dates June 2025 to confirm whether the project reached full completion, and no data was found on ANPR-driven automated challan volumes actually issued in Guwahati to date — meaning it remains unclear whether this infrastructure is yet operating as an enforcement (versus pure-surveillance) system.
focus_areas.policy_willpower: The scale of committed capital (~₹220 crore) and the multi-agency coordination behind Guwahati's smart-camera project demonstrate real institutional willpower toward tech-enabled traffic and public-safety management in Assam's capital. However, the project is publicly framed as a general public-safety/smart-city initiative rather than an explicitly branded road-safety enforcement or ANPR-challan programme in the way SATARK is designed and marketed; no Assam legislative or budget item was found earmarking ANPR-based traffic-violation enforcement specifically, and no state statement was found expressing intent to partner with SATARK, Cars24, or Crashfree India on enforcement technology.
focus_areas.cfi_engagement: Assam does not appear among SATARK's live cities (Bengaluru, Gurugram, Jaipur) or its four underway cities (Pune, Rajkot, Gandhinagar, Thiruvananthapuram); no Cars24/Crashfree India engagement with Assam or Guwahati authorities on ANPR enforcement technology was found in any source searched.
